concepts.description: The interaction of supply and demand curves determines the equilibrium price and quantity in a competitive market. This framework is the foundation of the document's analysis.
concepts.name: Supply and Demand

concepts.description: The price and quantity at which supply equals demand, where neither buyers nor sellers have an incentive to change their behavior in a competitive market.
concepts.name: Equilibrium Price and Quantity

concepts.description: A measure of how responsive the quantity demanded is to a change in price. It indicates how sensitive consumers are to price changes.
concepts.name: Price Elasticity of Demand

concepts.description: Measures of economic welfare: consumer surplus is the benefit buyers receive above what they pay, and producer surplus is the amount sellers receive above their minimum acceptable price.
concepts.name: Consumer and Producer Surplus

concepts.description: Policies such as price floors, price ceilings, and taxes that alter market outcomes. The document notes these matter when they bind, meaning when they actually change the equilibrium.
concepts.name: Government Interventions in Markets

concepts.description: The loss of total surplus that occurs when a market intervention or distortion prevents mutually beneficial transactions from taking place.
concepts.name: Deadweight Loss
